narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story and introduces each speech.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God, answering Job out of the whirlwind and judging the friends.

job.name: Job
job.note: The just man of Hus, afflicted and now humbled before the Lord.

1.t: Then Job answered the Lord, and said:

2.t: I know that thou canst do all things, and no thought is hid from thee.

3.t: Who is this that hideth counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken unwisely, and things that above measure exceeded my knowledge.

4.t: Hear, and I will speak: I will ask thee, and do thou tell me.

5.t: With the hearing of the ear, I have heard thee, but now my eye seeth thee.

6.t: Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in dust and ashes.

7.t: And after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Themanite:
My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends, because you have not spoken the thing that is right before me, as my servant Job hath.

8.t: Take unto you therefore seven oxen and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer for yourselves a holocaust, and my servant Job shall pray for you: his face I will accept, that folly be not imputed to you: for you have not spoken right things before me, as my servant Job hath.

9.t: So Eliphaz the Themanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite went, and did as the Lord had spoken to them, and the Lord accepted the face of Job.

10.t: The Lord also was turned at the penance of Job, when he prayed for his friends. And the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

11.t: And all his brethren came to him, and all his sisters, and all that knew him before, and they ate bread with him in his house: and bemoaned him, and comforted him upon all the evil that God had brought upon him. And every man gave him one ewe, and one earring of gold.

12.t: And the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. And he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

13.t: And he had seven sons, and three daughters.

14.t: And he called the name of one Dies, and the name of the second Cassia, and the name of the third Cornustibii.

15.t: And there were not found in all the earth women so beautiful as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

16.t: And Job lived after these things, a hundred and forty years, and he saw his children, and his children's children, unto the fourth generation, and he died an old man, and full of days.
